::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
## What you will do

1. Install R and an IDE (Positron or RStudio).
2. Install the R packages used in EPI 553.
3. Make a project folder for the course.
4. Render the setup check file to confirm that everything works.

Allow about 30 minutes. Do this before the first lab.
:::

## 1. Install R and an IDE

1. **R** (version 4.4 or later): download it from [CRAN](https://cloud.r-project.org/) for Windows, Mac, or Linux and install it with the default options.
2. **An IDE**, either one:
   - **Positron** (recommended): [positron.posit.co](https://positron.posit.co/). A modern IDE from Posit for R and Python. Quarto is built in.
   - **RStudio Desktop**: [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/). The long-standing R IDE. Quarto is built in.

Both work for every lecture and lab. [Introduction to R](intro-to-r.qmd) shows where things are in each.

## 2. Install the course packages

Open your IDE, click in the **Console**, and run this once (it takes a few minutes):


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "rmarkdown", "knitr", "kableExtra", "broom", "gtsummary",
  "car", "ggeffects", "janitor", "plotly", "NHANES", "brfssdata", "corrplot"
))
```
:::


Later lectures load a few more packages; each lecture lists the ones it uses at the top, and you install any you are missing the same way.

::: {.callout-tip}
## About brfssdata

Several lectures use the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) through the [brfssdata](https://muntasirmasum.github.io/brfssdata/) package. The first time you call `read_brfss()` for a survey year, it downloads that year once (about 20 MB) and keeps it on your computer, so you need an internet connection only the first time.
:::

## 3. Make a project folder

Keep all your EPI 553 work in one folder, for example `Documents/EPI553`, with four subfolders:

```
EPI553/
  data/      raw and cleaned data files
  scripts/   .R scripts
  outputs/   rendered HTML files, tables
  figures/   saved plots
```

Open the folder as your workspace every time you work on the course:

- **Positron:** **File → Open Folder** and choose `EPI553`.
- **RStudio:** **File → New Project → Existing Directory** and choose `EPI553` (this creates `EPI553.Rproj`; open that file next time).

R then reads and writes files relative to this folder, so you never need `setwd()`.

## 4. Render the setup check

[Download the setup check (.qmd)](templates/template-setup-check.qmd){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-primary download="setup-check.qmd"}

1. Save `setup-check.qmd` in your `EPI553` folder and open it in your IDE.
2. Render it: the **Preview** button in Positron, or **Render** in RStudio.
3. The HTML report lists your R version, which course packages are installed, whether the four folders exist, and a test plot and model.

If every check passes, you are ready for the first lab. If a package is missing, run `install.packages("name")` for it and render again. If something else fails, send the HTML report (or a screenshot) to the instructor or TA through Brightspace, or bring it to office hours.
